newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sends four planes for Cambodia evacuation.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sends four planes for Cambodia evacuation.

text.p: Singapore has sent four C-130 aircraft to evacuate about 300 of its citizens, and some foreigners, from Cambodia, a source close to the operation told Reuters on Wednesday.
The source said the four planes left Singapore early Wednesday morning for Phnom Penh and the first aircraft arrived back in the city state at midday.
"The evacuation will take place throughout the day until all the Singaporeans who want to leave Cambodia are evacuated," the source said.

The aircraft are enough to evacuate more people than the 300 Singaporeans currently in Cambodia, and foreigners who have approached the Singapore government are also expected to be among the evacuees, the source said.

"Our first priority is to evacuate Singaporeans. But usually we give allowance for that (evacuation of foreigners)," the source said. Among the foreigners expected are a group of Bruneians who "have indicated they would like to be included" in the evacuation, the source said.
State television earlier reported the family of the Brunei ambassador to Cambodia would be among those evacuated.
Ministry of Defence officials had no immediate comment but said a statement would be issued later.
Fighting between rival factions of the country's co-prime ministers flared up in Cambodia over the weekend.
